description:
We are Team SiriusTa, tackling the Crop Rotation Challenge. Inspired by ancient Egyptian astronomical farming heritage, SiriusTa bridges NASA Earth observations (SMAP, ECOSTRESS, Landsat, GPM) with local soil data and farmer priorities.

Our mission is to build a simple, accessible decision-support tool that translates complex space data into practical crop-rotation strategies—helping smallholder farmers restore soil health, conserve water, and build climate resilience.
summary: Farmers are making consequential decisions in a climate that is moving outside historical norms, usually without plot-level information on soil water, crop stress, or approaching hazards. SiriusTa gives every registered plot a Land ID, fuses NASA Earth observations with climate, soil, and market data, and delivers simple green/yellow/red guidance through a smartphone app Its distinguishing idea is a cross-regional network: plots with similar environmental profiles are linked, so what is learned about stress and risk in one region can inform calibrated warnings in another.
details:
What we built SiriusTa is an agro-satellite intelligence web application that takes any field coordinate on Earth and returns a visual field report together with a full dual-coordinate agronomic examination.
A user enters a latitude/longitude (by picking a city, using GPS, or typing exact coordinates) and names the previous harvested crop.
The engine then resolves the soil, terrain and climate of that point, ingests 45 days of live satellite telemetry, conditions the time series, and produces a three-tier decision report covering immediate field actions, two multi-season crop-rotation plans, and a global teleconnection-adjusted scoring of those plans. It finally matches the target field to the nearest peer agro-zone and runs the same pipeline on that twin, producing a normalized agronomic-similarity score and a delta/parity report.
Problem it solves Smallholder and commercial farmers rarely have access to an integrated view of their field that combines soil chemistry, recent weather, vegetation vigour and large-scale climate teleconnections in one place. Decisions about irrigation, fertilisation, pest pressure and crop rotation are made on partial information. SiriusTa addresses this by fusing multiple public satellite and soil data sources into a single, actionable per-field recommendation
SiriusTa directly uses three NASA datasets — NASA POWER climatology, NASA POWER daily agro-meteorological telemetry, and NASA MODIS NDVI vegetation imagery — as the scientific backbone of every recommendation. NASA POWER defines the Agro-Ecological Zone (AEZ) of the field, the 45-day dynamic window drives a coupled soil-water and nitrogen mass-balance, and MODIS NDVI anchors the vegetation-vigour layer. These NASA inputs feed a deterministic decision engine that turns raw Earth-observation data into concrete, field-level adaptation advice: how much to irrigate, whether to plant a cover crop, how to manage nutrition and insecticide, and which crop sequence to follow over the next three seasons.
